title: Longitudinal pulmonary imaging and assessment of lung function of former very preterm infants - Pulmonary trajectories following prematurity – PRIORITY Development in premature infants at the age of 12
summary: To describe the pulmonary changes in former premature infants and to identify the characteristics of those infants who are most severely affected by impaired lung function. In addition, we are investigating the effects on the cardiovascular system of these children. Of particular importance is that we want to link structural and functional lung changes with differences in the microbial epigenetic-immune-metabolic profile. In particular, we want to take into account sex specific differences in connection with the cause of prematurity . Finally, the study aims to specify the changes over time from the pre-adolescent phase to adulthood.
conditions: Bronchopulmonary dysplasia originating in the perinatal period

interventions.name:
Former very low birth weight (VLBW) infants born before the completed 32nd week of gestation at the LMU hospital perinatal center at the age of 12 and 18 years will be examined at the ages of 12 and 18:
- Lung function testing including:
   - Spirometry
   - assessment of lung volumes
   - lung

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Former VLBW infants born before the completed 32nd week of gestation at the LMU hospital perinatal center as well as term born infants at the age of 12 years.
Exclusion criteria:
• No parental or caregivers´ consent. 
• Severe neurologic impairment that does not allow lung function and exercise capacity testing. 
• Severe congenital malformation according to the international classification 
(excluding inguinal hernia, PDA, atrial septal defects, ventricular septal defects and all congenital anomalies that do not affect pulmonary, cardiovascular and psychomotor capacities). 
• Oligohydramnios before 22 weeks´ gestation.
